decisions.reason: The local class included u(x)=1/(1-x) on (-1,1), contradicting the finite-scaled-norm ball supplier. C^{k,alpha} now denotes finite full-domain norm, C_b is its alias, and C_loc denotes local regularity. Norms, boundary-extension class and domain charts are preserved (a local chart can be shrunk to have finite norm).

F8 falsely attributed a global endpoint convention and Lipschitz-to-beta inclusion to a definition restricted to interior balls and 0<alpha<1. The convention is now declared locally, sourced to the actual global convention in F7 for alpha<1, and step 3.3 proves the endpoint inclusion by splitting distances at 1. The classical and distributional formulas, angular cancellation and correction sign remain valid.

With X=Y={0} a negative C satisfies the stated estimate but contradicts the inverse-norm bound. The estimate constant is now explicitly nonnegative, preserving C=0 and proving that case forces both spaces to be zero. The closedness proof and Neumann-series argument apply for C>0; the endpoint supremum argument now uses closedness before treating t=1.

F3 incorrectly required domination of integrands alone. Its actual application in step 2.3 already bounds every parameter derivative by a constant times |g(y)| on a separated compact support, hence meets the true differentiation theorem. F3 now states derivative domination and the dominated-convergence continuity condition. Steps 2.1 and 3.1 independently justify the C1 formula and divergent second difference quotient by integrable kernel error bounds.

On the rejected carrier C^{0,alpha}(B) meant only local regularity, so the bounded smooth elliptic coefficient 2+sin(1/(1-x))/2 had that membership without a finite full-ball seminorm. The supplier notation is now consistent, and this remark explicitly requires [A]_{0,alpha;B}<=K<infinity and distinguishes C_loc. The ellipticity, frozen operator, and Definition section are unchanged.

The blanket boundary-seminorm incompleteness claim is false: for k=0 on (0,1), a seminorm-Cauchy sequence has convergent endpoint differences and hence a limit in that seminorm. The correct caveat is failure to be a norm, since constants lie in its kernel. Uniform limits of all derivative fields, identification along coordinate segments, and passage of difference quotients prove the full-norm completeness and closed zero-boundary subspace without this false caveat. Local notation is reconciled with the repaired definition.

F3 falsely said that arbitrary alpha-Holder compositions preserve the exponent; t^alpha composed with itself gives t^(alpha squared). Every inner map actually used is a shear or its inverse with a bounded gradient and hence is Lipschitz. F3 now proves the correct composition and product bounds. The chain-rule pullback matrix J^{-1} A J^{-T}, drift correction sign, image patch and ellipticity constants are unchanged and valid.

The matrix Hessian identity in F4 incorrectly replaced the two transposed mixed terms by twice one tensor. It now has Deta tensor Dw plus Dw tensor Deta, componentwise from the weak product rule. The operator commutator keeps its factor 2 because A is symmetric; each Hessian mixed term has the same norm bound, so the freezing, finite-overlap cover and hole-filling proof need no further change.

Step 1.1 omitted K||D2g||_infinity and [b]_alpha||Dg||_infinity from the Holder product bound; A=I, b=x1 e1 and g=x1 on B_epsilon refute it. The repaired bound retains both terms and both factors for every lower-order product. Finite boundary charts control [g]_alpha and [Dg]_alpha by the full C2alpha norm with a domain-dependent constant. This preserves the theorem and completes the zero-boundary reduction.

F4 omitted zeroth- and first-order integrability from the W2p definition. It now states all orders through two, and isolates the necessary condition actually used. The sector Hessian has Frobenius norm sqrt(2) gamma(1-gamma) r^(gamma-2), whose pth power with polar weight r is nonintegrable exactly at p>=2/(2-gamma). Since any weak Hessian must equal the classical Hessian on the open sector, this excludes W2p without needing to assert first-derivative integrability for every p.

The final remark falsely claimed exactly the strictly subcritical Holder exponents. The actual embedding includes the nonintegral endpoint, so p>n gives C^{1,1-n/p}, including C^{1,1/2} for p=2n. The sufficient strict ranges in the Statement and proof remain correct; the remark now records the stronger supplier endpoint without calling the weaker ranges optimal.

The actual prerequisite proof explicitly supplies the missing quantitative input: thm-weak-global-w-two-p-dirichlet-regularity-for-the-laplacian F2 gives shifted W2q strong solvability and its norm bound for every 1<q<infinity; steps 1.1-3.1 use the same finite exponent list and energy uniqueness. The consumer explicitly cites that proof, rather than claiming its final p>n statement covers each intermediate q. The initial H1 bound controls Lq0, each embedding controls the next Lq, and a fixed shift and finite list give uniform constants independent of epsilon. Haller-Dintelmann Theorem 19.7 confirms the strong solvability and estimates on bounded C2 domains. The original item is mathematically sound and was restored byte for byte.
